notes.text: Bowen Byram is day to day (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 6 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Wyatt Kaiser has taken his spot beside Artyom Levshunov.

They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen in 9 of their last 10 games, including the last one. Dominic James takes shifts on two lines, L3 and L4. Ryan McDonagh is the seventh defenseman, rotating in mostly beside Moser and Lilleberg.
Yanni Gourde is on the injured non-roster list (hip surgery) and has not played this season.

story.head: Mikheyev meets his old team
paras: The Blackhawks (4-9-0) lost 4-1 to Detroit on Oct 29, while the Lightning (8-3-1) beat Winnipeg 6-4 the same night. The Blackhawks played last night, and the Lightning are rested. Going in, the Blackhawks are last in the Central (31st in the NHL) and the Bolts fourth in the Atlantic (tied for tenth).

The Blackhawks have played better than their record (.308) says: their chances are worth about .368, and their finishing has held them back. The Lightning’s record (.708) is about what their chances are worth.

The Blackhawks do a lot of their shooting from distance (2nd lowest) and don't block many shots (32nd). They also have struggled on the power play (32nd), so their struggling power play gets a tough test from the Lightning’s penalty killers. Chicago has scored 2.08 goals a game, the second fewest in the league, and allowed 3.69, the fourth most. As for the Lightning, they get into more chippy games than anyone (1st), rarely ice the puck (2nd) and keep shots away from their net (3rd). The Lightning are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Blackhawks.

Patrick Kane (1 G / 7 A / 8 P in 13 GP) leads the Blackhawks in scoring, and Roman Kantserov (5 G / 1 A / 6 P in 13 GP) has a team-high five goals. For the Lightning, Brandon Hagel (8 G / 8 A / 16 P in 12 GP) leads the way in scoring. Nikita Kucherov (4 G / 11 A / 15 P in 12 GP) isn’t far behind, with seven points in his last five games and a point in six straight games against Chicago.

Andrei Vasilevskiy (6-3-0 / .876 SV% in 9 GS) will likely start for Tampa Bay. Chicago has two options in net: Spencer Knight (4-7-0 / .897 SV% in 11 GS) and Arvid Söderblom (0-2-0 / .820 SV% in 2 GS). Knight has started nine of their last ten games, including the last one on Oct 29, so Chicago could turn to Söderblom to give him a rest. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.

At home, Jon Cooper likes to send Hagel, Cirelli and Holmberg out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Kantserov, Bedard and Teräväinen. Elsewhere, the Lightning usually control more of the chances than the Blackhawks do.
